finding: This revision rewrote §1 item 1 and appended the new claim "§2.4 states those five conditions normatively; this sentence summarises them and adds nothing." The summary does not match condition 2. §2.4 condition 2 reads "holds at least one non-PASS row **not** attributed to `spec-coverage` — including any row carrying no role", while §1 renders it as "while other roles still hold open findings". §2.4 line 133 explicitly identifies that exact wording as false in a state condition 2 admits: the third `message` form exists because "the first clause of the other two positively asserts the findings are open *from other roles*, which is false exactly when no role holds any", and test 17 pins that fixture (`open_roles` is `[]`, every open row carries no role). So in the one state §2.4 gives a dedicated message form for, §1's summary is false while asserting it adds nothing. This is the same failure shape as the four high findings the round-8 revision just eliminated between §4 sentence 5 and the §2.6 `hint` — a section claiming textual identity/equivalence with a normative section it does not actually match — reintroduced in a different section by the change that was fixing the condition count.

finding: The round-8 finding on cause precedence ("the four no-rows causes are not mutually exclusive and no precedence is stated ... the two print different text over identical state — a determinism gap") was closed by adding a normative rule: "their evaluation order is fixed: the stored-`roles_hash` comparison is decided first ... and the remaining three follow in the order of the table below. The first cause that applies is the one named." No test was added with it. §6 test 9 still instantiates one cause per fixture ("a deleted file, a round entry with an empty `file`, a file holding a line that does not unmarshal ..., and an earlier round whose stored `roles_hash` differs"), and no other §6 item exercises a round to which two causes apply. The co-applying state is reachable without hand-editing: an earlier round whose recorded `audit-round-N.ndjson` was deleted, sitting below a corpus edit made between rounds, satisfies cause 2 and cause 4 at once. Table-order-first emits `round <N> file <name> is missing; skipping its rows` and the specified order emits `round <N> was recorded under a different auditor corpus; skipping its rows`; both pass every test in §6. The original finding's own closing sentence — "Test 9 exercises one cause per fixture and cannot pin the choice" — is therefore still true, so the determinism gap §1's second constraint forbids survives the fix in the observable bytes.

finding: Condition 5 is specified as "engine.RolesStale ... is false", used verbatim. RolesStale exempts an empty stored hash (internal/engine/reviewstate.go:281-285: `if stored == "" { return false }`) — exactly the exemption §2.1 rejects for its own corpus comparison, on the stated ground that "tp does not know which panel that round used, and ending the walk is the reading §1 requires". The two rules therefore disagree about the same state. When the LATEST recorded round carries an empty roles_hash — the ComputeRolesHash-error path §2.1 itself names, since internal/engine/rolehash.go:61 returns ("", err) on an unreadable role file and both audit callers discard the error — no corpus check reaches that round at all: §2.1's fourth cause only compares EARLIER rounds against the latest, and condition 5 reads false by exemption. If every round of an audit was recorded while a role file was unreadable, all stored hashes are equal (""), cause 4 never fires, condition 5 is permanently false, and `divergence` fires at full streak length over a corpus tp cannot identify and whose movement it cannot detect — the direction §1 forbids. Test 12 pins only the non-empty-stored-hash half.

finding: Condition 5 needs a CURRENT auditor-corpus hash, and on the --record path no such value exists where the signal is computed: ComputeRolesHash is called inside the round-recording helper (internal/cli/audit_record.go:106) and its result is stamped on the round entry but never returned to the caller, which has no rolesHash variable (unlike runAuditStatus, which computes one at line 187 for roles_stale). §2.4 gives two rules that point in different directions: condition 5 "is false by construction" on --record, and condition 5 "mirrors condition 3 exactly", where condition 3 "is evaluated the same way on both and must not be wired to a different staleness source on either". The implementer must choose between threading the stamped hash out of the recording helper, making a second full ComputeRolesHash call, and skipping the evaluation — and the three differ observably: if a role file becomes unreadable between the stamp and a second call, ComputeRolesHash returns "" with an error both audit callers discard, RolesStale then compares the round's non-empty stored hash against "" and reads true, withholding divergence; the threaded-hash and skip variants emit it. §1's fail-toward-keep-auditing constraint picks the withholding branch, but the spec never says so, and §2.2's cost paragraph — which pins every other extra read this release adds so "the cost is not restated as zero" — does not mention a second corpus read on --record.

finding: §3.1 defines "mechanized" as "a valid checks entry's class equals it exactly" with no exemption, and §3.2 then excludes every mechanized class from mechanize_candidates. The class `over-specification` satisfies ValidateChecks' `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, so an operator may register a check for it — after which §3.2 silently removes it from mechanize_candidates and §3.3 lists it in mechanized_classes as "withheld because mechanized". That contradicts an invariant this spec never says it changes: engine.OverSpecificationClass is documented as "the un-mechanizable finding class" whose recurring instances "may still appear in the frequency-only mechanize_candidates array", excluded only from next_action branch 3 (internal/engine/nextaction.go:9-13). The same registration also puts `over-specification` on the reviewer exclusion list ("do NOT report findings of these classes") in the very prompt that appends the canonical-class instruction telling reviewers to raise it (internal/cli/review.go:944) — one prompt asserting both. No Non-Goal covers this, and §3.1's claim of a single governing definition makes the collision invisible to an implementer.

finding: This revision replaced the (incorrect) "at both sites the surrounding branch ... keeps its existing guard" with a site-specific rule: "At the regression site one `if len(checks) > 0` block both runs the mechanical checks and appends the sentence, so the block stays and the append inside it becomes conditional on the post-drop list. At the panel site the check run and the sentence sit behind two independent guards ... and only the sentence's changes." The code confirms the asymmetry (internal/cli/review_regression.go:94-101 is one block; internal/cli/review.go:466 and :794 are independent guards in two functions), and it means the failure mode §3.2 forbids — "a workflow whose entries are all invalid still runs the checks, still emits each entry's skip notice, and still renders `mechanical_checks` as it does today" — is reachable at the regression site only. §6 does not pin it there. Test 39 ("When every registered entry is invalid, prompt emission appends no such sentence at all ... and the same payload still renders `mechanical_checks` as it does today") names no site, and test 40 covers both sites only for the drop-an-invalid-entry case with a valid entry surviving. An implementation that moves the whole regression-site guard to the post-drop list — the natural reading of "when the drop empties the list, the sentence is not appended at all" — stops running the checks there and flips `mechanical_checks` from `[]` to null, and passes tests 39 and 40 if test 39 is written against the panel site. That is exactly the consequence the accepted round-7 finding on this paragraph named.

finding: Test 36 ("A registered check whose command fails still suppresses its class, asserted with a check whose command exits non-zero") never names the mode it is asserted on, and the obvious reading makes the fixture vacuous. §3.3 says `mechanize_candidates`/`mechanized_classes` are emitted on `tp review <spec> --record` and nowhere else, while §3.1 states that "`tp review --record` executes no check at all" — so on `--record` the registered command is never executed and a non-zero-exiting entry is byte-for-byte indistinguishable from a passing one. An engineer writing the test on `--record` proves nothing about §3.2's "Whether the registered check passes is irrelevant"; another engineer writing it on `tp review <spec> --status --check` (where §3.2 says a failing check is reported in `mechanical_checks` and gates the exit code) or on prompt emission asserts a genuinely different observable. Two contradictory tests both satisfy the sentence as written.

finding: Tests 9 and 10 pin the four no-rows advisories on an EARLIER recorded round, but state only one of the two preconditions such a fixture must satisfy. Test 10 says only "the fixture must place the no-rows round below the just-recorded one". §2.2's walk-stop rule means the walk descends from round N to round N-1 only when at least one role present in round N is clean in round N (all its rows PASS); a fixture whose just-recorded round N carries a non-PASS row for every role closes every streak at N and never reads N-1, so no advisory fires and a CORRECT implementation fails the test. Second, §2.1 fixes cause 4 (stored roles_hash) as the first cause evaluated, so a hand-built round N-1 whose stored roles_hash does not equal round N's emits the corpus wording rather than the missing-file / empty-file / unparseable wording the test asserts — and an empty stored hash on a legacy fixture round is a difference under the deliberate plain-inequality rule. Test 9 has the same two gaps for its first three causes.

finding: §2's row-role rule makes every trimmed non-empty `role` string a role id, and grounds itself on "the trim-then-drop-empty rule OverlapReport already applies" — but OverlapReport also drops the reserved regression id (internal/engine/overlap.go:47), and §2 never says whether that reserved id is a role for §2's purposes. The consequence is concrete and lands inside one payload: a non-PASS row carrying `"role":"regression"` in an audit results file would produce a role_streaks entry, be named in divergence.open_roles and counted in other_roles_open, while the sibling overlap_report in the same --status payload silently discards it — the exact kind of disagreement §2.2 spends a paragraph reconciling for the two arrays. Nothing in the audit prompt path emits that id (audit has no regression role), so the row can only come from a sub-agent that wrote it anyway, which is precisely the input §2.1's other rules are written to survive.

finding: §2.1's fifth governing definition asserts "Every value in §2 is computed from it [the walked segment] alone, and no rule anywhere requires reading the whole recorded history" — and §2.1 opens by saying none of the five definitions may be restated differently anywhere else. §2.4 then does restate it differently: conditions 3, 4 and 5 are computed outside the walked segment, from the round index and the latest round's stored hashes, and §2.4 says so itself — "engine.ConsecutiveClean walks the stored per-round clean boolean", which reaches rounds below where §2.2's walk stopped (test 13's fixture stops the walk at round 4 while `converged` still reads rounds 1-3). The emission of `divergence` is a value in §2 and it does depend on that history.

finding: The new sentence added to close the round-8 finding that `role_streaks[].open` is "defended nowhere as a magnitude" reads: "`open` earns its place the other way round: its boolean content duplicates the streak, but its magnitude does not, and it is the only per-role attribution of `divergence.other_roles_open` the payload carries." finding: `role_streaks` is the only array this release adds whose empty shape is not pinned against the nil-slice serialization the spec itself calls a recorded defect class. §2.4 pins `open_roles` as "`[]` when empty, never `null` and never omitted"; §3.3 pins `mechanized_classes` and the filtered `mechanize_candidates` as "an emitted empty array, not an absent key and not `null`", and test 37 calls that the discriminating half; §2.3 pins `spec_coverage_clean_rounds` as "an explicit JSON null, never an omitted key". §2.2 says only that `role_streaks` "is `[]` whenever no role appears in the latest recorded audit round", and test 14 restates the same phrasing ("`role_streaks` is `[]`"). finding: The reviewer-exclusion paragraph narrates the current shape of the two emission sites rather than the behaviour they must produce: "At the regression site one `if len(checks) > 0` block both runs the mechanical checks and appends the sentence, so the block stays and the append inside it becomes conditional on the post-drop list. At the panel site the check run and the sentence sit behind two independent guards of the same shape in two functions, and only the sentence's changes." Both halves are accurate against the tree today (review_regression.go's single `if len(wfChecks.Checks) > 0` block runs the checks and appends the sentence; review.go's append sits in its own guard), which is exactly the problem — the sentences are a diff instruction whose correctness can only be established against code, and they buy nothing the durable rules beside them do not already give: the same paragraph already states that only the sentence's own guard moves to the post-drop list, and §3.2's next paragraph already states that both sites change. The observable requirements are then pinned by tests 38, 39 and 40. This is spec altitude spent on edit mechanism a task's acceptance should own; it also dates the spec to one refactor of either function.

finding: Non-Goal 9 grounds the exclusion of `tp review --report` on "Every other mode takes the spec as a positional, and workflow resolution uses it as an anchor".
